This article compares the demographic and clinical characteristics of newly diagnosed and prevalent children and adolescents with [[inflammatoriske-tarmsygdomme|Inflammatoriske tarmsygdomme]] (IBD) who had at least one hospital contact between October 1, 2022, and September 30, 2023 [^src1]. Analyzing these cohorts is essential for understanding the current burden of pediatric IBD and for planning specialized gastroenterology resources.

In terms of overall volume, the prevalent group is the clear leader, comprising 551 patients, while the newly diagnosed group accounts for 189 patients [^src1]. Across both cohorts, [[crohns-sygdom|Crohns sygdom]] is the leading diagnosis, affecting 57% (107 patients) of the newly diagnosed and 55% (305 patients) of the prevalent population [^src1]. [[colitis-ulcerosa|Colitis ulcerosa]] is the second most common condition, representing 42% (80 patients) of new cases and 44% (245 patients) of prevalent cases [^src1]. Primary sclerosing cholangitis acts as a significant outlier and trailer, with only 1 newly diagnosed case and 0 prevalent cases recorded during this period [^src1].

Demographically, boys lead in both groups, making up 61% (116 patients) of newly diagnosed and 53% (291 patients) of prevalent patients, compared to girls at 39% (73 patients) and 47% (260 patients) [^src1]. The prevalent cohort is slightly older, with a mean age of 14 years (range 2-17) and a median of 15 years, whereas the newly diagnosed group has a mean age of 13 years (range 0-17) and a median of 14 years [^src1]. The oldest age bracket (15-17 years) dominates both groups, representing 50% (94 patients) of new diagnoses and 60% (333 patients) of prevalent cases [^src1]. Conversely, the youngest age group (0-4 years) is the trailer, comprising just 5% (9 patients) of new cases and 1% (5 patients) of prevalent cases [^src1].

Regarding healthcare utilization, newly diagnosed patients average slightly more contacts (17, range 1-49) than prevalent patients (15, range 1-47) [^src1]. Physical attendance is the leading contact type across the board, accounting for 63% (1,188 contacts) of interactions for newly diagnosed patients and 67% (3,496 contacts) for prevalent patients, while virtual contacts make up the remaining 37% (709 contacts) and 33% (1,742 contacts), respectively [^src1].

Because the provided data covers only a single reporting period (October 2022 to September 2023), no longitudinal trends or changes over time can be established from this dataset alone. Furthermore, the source tables do not record any specific clinical targets, thresholds, or standards that would allow for an assessment of targets met or missed.

Summary: Tabellen sammenligner karakteristika for nydiagnosticerede og prævalente børn og unge med IBD, herunder diagnosefordeling, køn, alder og kontakttype, og viser at både grupper domineres af Crohns sygdom, drenge og aldersgruppen 15–17 år.
